title: Produced-Water Lithium
question: Which U.S. basins have analyzed produced-water wells meeting a lithium screening rule, how much of that picture reflects sampling and compilation, and how well do predictions transfer to held-out basins?
one_liner: The USGS National Produced Waters Geochemical Database v3.0, a pre-registered screening rule with cited thresholds, dataset-clustered bootstrap intervals, a missingness audit, and lithium prediction evaluated by random folds, leave-one-dataset-out and leave-one-basin-out.
aim: Rank U.S. basins by the fraction of produced-water wells meeting a cited lithium-extraction screen, test whether the ranking is an artifact of how the USGS produced-waters database was compiled, characterise which rows have lithium measured, and test whether lithium can be predicted where it was not measured.
hypothesis: Pre-registered rules: the ranking is robust to compilation bias if removing the four lithium-focused source datasets leaves at least four of the top five basins and reverses no separable pair; lithium measurement is not missing at random if a classifier separates measured from unmeasured rows with AUC at least 0.70; prediction is useful out of basin if leave-one-basin-out R-squared is at least 0.30 and AUC at the screening floor at least 0.75.
conclusion: The database carries no detection-limit information; below-detection and not-analyzed cells are indistinguishable. {{screen.n_pass_primary}} of {{screen.n_li_wells}} lithium wells pass the screen. {{screen.n_basins_frac_interval_excludes_zero}} ranked basins have screened-fraction intervals excluding zero; the highest median is supported by one dataset with centroid coordinates. Removing named lithium-focused datasets leaves the ranking robust under the frozen rule, but within-basin dataset medians differ by a median factor of {{screen.ds.median_ratio:.1f}}. Lithium measurement is associated with observed row characteristics. Out-of-basin prediction error is {{model.rmse_ratio_lobo_random_hgb:.2f}} times the random-fold error; it passes the pooled pre-registered rule but screening precision is {{model.lobo.hgb.cls_precision:.2f}} and only {{model.lobo.hgb.n_basins_r2_ge_0_3}} of {{model.n_basins_heldout}} basins meet the R-squared bar.

finding: Non-detects are not represented at all in version 3.0. Lithium has {{nondetect.Li.nonempty}} non-empty cells with {{nondetect.Li.negative}} negative, {{nondetect.Li.zero}} zero and {{nondetect.Li.lt_prefixed}} less-than values, and the dictionary has {{nondetect.dictionary_detection_fields}} detection fields of {{nondetect.dictionary_fields}}. A below-detection result is an empty cell, indistinguishable from not analysed. That is the first finding, and it means every lithium value here is a detection.

With a floor of {{screen.floor_mg_l:.0f}} mg/L and a magnesium-to-lithium ceiling of {{screen.ceiling_mg_li:.0f}}, both cited, {{screen.n_above_floor}} of {{screen.n_li_wells}} lithium wells clear the floor and {{screen.n_pass_primary}} pass the joint screen. Of {{screen.n_basins_ranked}} basins with at least {{screen.min_wells_basin}} wells, {{screen.n_basins_frac_interval_excludes_zero}} have screened-fraction intervals that exclude zero: {{screen.pass1.name}} ({{screen.pass1.frac_pass:.0%}} of {{screen.pass1.n_wells}} wells, one dataset, all centroid coordinates), {{screen.pass2.name}} ({{screen.pass2.frac_pass:.0%}} of {{screen.pass2.n_wells}}) and {{screen.pass3.name}} ({{screen.pass3.frac_pass:.1%}} of {{screen.pass3.n_wells}}). Removing the four datasets the compilers named as lithium-focused removes only {{screen.adj.n_li_wells_removed}} lithium wells and leaves the top five unchanged, so the ranking is robust to that bias. The subtler batch effect is larger: within basins with more than one source dataset, dataset medians differ by a median factor of {{screen.ds.median_ratio:.1f}} and up to {{screen.ds.max_ratio:.0f}}.

Lithium was measured on {{miss.share_measured:.1%}} of rows and a classifier tells measured from unmeasured rows with an AUC of {{miss.auc:.2f}}; {{miss.datasets_none_measured}} of {{miss.datasets_total}} source datasets never measured it, and {{miss.decade_top_measured_share:.0%}} of dated lithium rows are from the 1960s. Prediction from major ions, depth and play type reaches an RMSE of {{model.random.hgb.rmse_pooled:.2f}} log units under random folds, {{model.lodo.hgb.rmse_pooled:.2f}} when whole source datasets are held out and {{model.lobo.hgb.rmse_pooled:.2f}} when whole basins are, with held-out R-squared falling from {{model.random.hgb.r2_pooled:.2f}} to {{model.lobo.hgb.r2_pooled:.2f}}. Precision at the screening floor falls from {{model.random.hgb.cls_precision:.2f}} to {{model.lobo.hgb.cls_precision:.2f}} out of basin. The positive control, predicting total dissolved solids from the same features, holds up out of basin (R-squared {{control.lobo.hgb.r2_pooled:.2f}}), so the pipeline can learn what is learnable.

The supplementary held-basin calibration audit finds a supported gap in {{domain_calibration.worst_lobo.domain}}: mean probability {{domain_calibration.worst_lobo.predicted:.1%}}, observed Li-floor exceedance {{domain_calibration.worst_lobo.observed:.1%}} on {{domain_calibration.worst_lobo.n}} wells. The observed-frequency Wilson interval is {{domain_calibration.worst_lobo.lo:.1%}} to {{domain_calibration.worst_lobo.hi:.1%}}. This selected diagnostic concerns the lithium floor alone, not the joint screen; it is not a formal calibration test.

traps.how: Version 3.0 added datasets because they were lithium-rich; the ranking was recomputed without them. Only {{screen.adj.n_li_wells_removed}} wells moved and the top five held, but within-basin dataset medians still differ by a median factor of {{screen.ds.median_ratio:.1f}}.

Holding out whole source datasets raises prediction RMSE from {{model.random.hgb.rmse_pooled:.2f}} to {{model.lodo.hgb.rmse_pooled:.2f}}; the fold range runs from {{model.lodo.hgb.rmse_fold_min:.2f}} to {{model.lodo.hgb.rmse_fold_max:.2f}}.
Leave-one-basin-out is the spatial analogue here: precision at the screening floor drops from {{model.random.hgb.cls_precision:.2f}} to {{model.lobo.hgb.cls_precision:.2f}}.
The database has no detection-limit representation at all; below-detection and not-analysed are the same empty cell. Reported as a finding rather than modelled.

Lithium is measured on {{miss.share_measured:.1%}} of rows and the measured rows are distinguishable from the rest (AUC {{miss.auc:.2f}}); bootstrap intervals resample wells clustered by dataset, not rows.
Repeated samples from one well are collapsed to the well before any count; a planted duplicate is tested.
